title: Offboarding sequences its parameter changes so that no user is liquidated on terms announced after the fact
content:
A.3.7.1.5.2.1 and A.3.7.1.5.2.2 define an ordered sequence for offboarding a permissionless collateral or vault type:

1. Set the debt ceiling to zero, so no new exposure can be created from the moment the decision is approved.
2. Make an initial public announcement across every channel listed in the Communication Channels Active Data.
3. Make a second announcement on the same channels "no later than 14 calendar days after the initial" one.
4. Only "once the second public announcements have been made, set the liquidation penalty to 0%."
5. Parameter changes that actually push users out — "such as changes to the liquidation ratio or stability fee" — may be implemented only after a further 14 calendar days have passed following the second announcement.

The ordering encodes the protection. Stopping new debt is instant because it harms nobody already in a position. Everything that could *cause* a liquidation is deferred behind two notices and a full 14-day window, so the earliest a user can be squeezed out is roughly a month after the first warning.

Step 4's placement is the subtle one: zeroing the liquidation penalty is a benefit to users, yet it is deliberately withheld until the second announcement has gone out — the announcements are the gating event that proves notice was given, and the sequence is written so a change of any kind marks a completed communication step.

A.3.7.1.5.3 keeps the channel list itself as Active Data maintained by Core GovOps under a Direct Edit protocol, so the notice obligation tracks whatever channels are current — Forum first, then calendars, Discord and Reddit, then direct outreach by Partner Relationship Leads to affected collateral partners and frontend providers.
description: The debt ceiling drops to zero immediately, two announcements follow at least 14 days apart, the penalty goes to 0% only after the second, and offboarding parameter changes wait 14 more days.
